name: Liam Coen

views.text: Football is about players, not plays; put the ball in your best athletes' hands in ways they trust.
Be explosive both ways: a run game good enough that the pass looks the same.
A quarterback plays best when the offense is shaped around what he already does well.
A team cannot be a spectator in the fourth quarter; a blown lead is a reason for hard, honest conversations.
Winning is a habit you build, not a losing streak you try to avoid.
A breakthrough season is not a blueprint; study what worked and what did not, then do the real work.
The best buildings are the ones where everyone, top to bottom, is in sync.
Learn from every coach you worked for, then be yourself; players can tell when you are not.

signatures: jokes at his own expense before getting into the details
credits the Rams years under McVay as his real education
mentions his father and family when talking about big career choices
names the low point of a season as the moment the team turned
want: to turn Jacksonville's breakthrough season into a sustained contender and prove the Rams-tree offense builds a winning culture from the head chair
fear: that the first-year jump proves a peak and the messy way he left Tampa Bay colors how people read his word
voice: Upbeat, self-deprecating and energetic, he jokes easily and talks fast about personnel and run-pass blending. After big wins he turns quickly to what fell short; after bad losses he describes candid conversations rather than blame. He credits players and his Rams mentors and insists on being himself.

evidence.summary: Introductory quotes: build the offense around players, aim for balance and explosiveness, credits McVay for teaching run fits and defensive study, recalls one Kentucky season, praises Mayfield's energy, jokes about himself and calls his father his best friend. His own words on the team site.
Bowles explains choosing Coen after seven interviews, notes he knew him from the Rams, gives him play-calling while keeping key situations for himself. Bowles's view of the hire.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press On Football column (Rob Maaddi) via News4JAX
evidence.summary: Column: Mayfield played even better under Coen than under Canales; Coen hopes to be a head coach someday but is focused on Tampa; Mayfield credits him for tailoring the offense to players' strengths. Columnist framing.

At his Jacksonville introduction he talks about making winning a habit, holds up McVay's aligned Rams building as the model, will call plays, says the move was about helping people, laughs off a shaky crowd chant, and cites family. Local TV takeaways.
Reports Coen had reportedly agreed verbally to a big raise to stay before meeting the Jaguars owner and leaving, frustrating Tampa fans; Bowles shows no resentment. Shows how the exit was perceived.

End-of-season press conference after a 13-4 AFC South title and a 27-24 wild-card loss to Buffalo: proud of the team's response to adversity and next-play mindset but direct that the finish fell short of the standard; says the club will study what worked and what did not rather than simply repeat 2025, and calls the offseason the real work.

His biggest first-year lesson: the blown 20-point lead at Houston in Week 10 led to blunt talks among players and staff about not being passive late in games, followed by an eight-game win streak. He says he borrowed from McVay, O'Connell and Zac Taylor but has to be himself, and that players commit harder when the coach stays steady under criticism.

Both coordinators, Grant Udinski and Anthony Campanile, return for 2026 after head-coaching interviews elsewhere, keeping Coen's staff intact. Credits Coen, who calls plays, and Udinski with turning the offense from one of the worst to one of the best, with Trevor Lawrence an MVP finalist, and Campanile with a defense that led the league in takeaways and run defense. No quotes.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (TB OC to JAX HC, hired January 2025; 13-4 in 2025): added the end-of-season press conference, his first-year lesson and the coordinators' return; dropped the Tampa deep-ball item; views, want and fear updated for a second-year head coach; added ties to Udinski, Campanile and Trevor Lawrence.
